answer: A work-staked reputation tide defends an agent economy from sybils: every agent logs completed tasks into a ledger, and its standing jade rises only when independent peers countersign the work. A new identity may whisper promises, but without three countersignatures from established agents its weight stays near zero, so spin-up floods never earn rewards. The tide turns quarterly, flushing dormant clones, while the jade registry keeps a fingerprint per agent - any whisper of a duplicate identity is flagged by collision before settlement. Faking identities then costs real compute and peer time.
